Which rare-earth element, known for its red phosphorescence, is incorporated into certain television screens to produce vivid red color?
questions.explanation: Europium is a rare-earth element (lanthanide) that emits a characteristic red glow when excited, making it invaluable as a red phosphor in CRT and some modern display technologies. Its unique luminescent properties stem from its electron configuration, which allows specific energy transitions that release red-wavelength photons. Europium compounds are also used in anti-counterfeiting measures on euro banknotes, where they fluoresce under UV light.
